label: Essence as nature or quiddity: Essence is what a thing is, its nature or quiddity, contrasted with…
term: essence as nature or quiddity (Thomistic attribute readings)
definition: Essence is what a thing is, its nature or quiddity, contrasted with its act of being (esse). The statement that God is his own esse identifies these in its theological context; the words essence and esse alone do not make that identity hold. This sense is not Scott’s modal essence of an individual or the 1970 Gödel variant’s different essence definition.
note: A terminological stipulation for the existing attribute records, checked against the materialized q.3 a.4 contrast of what a thing is with its esse. No new Lean essence predicate or identity proof is introduced; sourcing a general essence theory remains separate from this vocabulary link. Lean locator: PrimaPars.Question3.Article4.Profile.essenceOf : Being → Principle is an existing primitive representation of nature, with the separately supplied esseOf field. Generic q.3/q.11 readings also take essenceOf as a parameter of that type. The field fixes neither a general essence theory nor the identity of essence and esse; those interpretive applications and open identity premises remain separate.
